cues.visual: Alice offers the two-rupee-and-one-paisa add-on and Bob buys it
cues.text: Alice prices an add-on at two rupees and one paisa. Payment APIs accept whole paise, not decimal rupees. Her integration must convert two point zero one into exactly two hundred and one.

cues.visual: The real Razorpay dashboard reveals the two-rupee order
cues.text: The request succeeds, but Razorpay's dashboard shows two rupees: two hundred paise. Razorpay stored what it received. Alice's one paisa vanished before the provider could know.

cues.visual: The generated floating-point conversion is revealed
cues.text: Now open the helper. It multiplies two point zero one by one hundred in binary floating point. The runtime gets two hundred point nine nine nine; integer conversion truncates it to two hundred.

cues.visual: Alice sees the silent one-paisa mutation
cues.text: The API receives an integer, so nothing crashes. Alice's amount became another order.

cues.visual: Bob has a green check while Alice questions the order's meaning
cues.text: Next Bob pays and receives a valid signature. He proves he paid Alice's order. Alice must still ask whether it means the purchase she intended.

cues.visual: The generated verifier binds only order ID and payment ID
cues.text: The verifier recomputes HMAC over order ID plus payment ID with Alice's secret. A match proves those identifiers belong together, nothing more.

cues.visual: Seller, amount, currency and cart are projected away
cues.text: Alice's promise also had seller, two hundred and one paise, currency, cart, and fulfil-once. None of those fields reaches this check.

cues.visual: A valid payment is contrasted with a wrong promise
cues.text: That is the semantic gap: cryptographic validity is not business correctness. A valid payment can settle the wrong order.

cues.visual: Alice takes the same checkout to JPY and KWD
cues.text: Now change currency. Bob pays yen or Kuwaiti dinar, but the same code multiplies both by one hundred.

cues.visual: The real provider table shows opposite currency corruptions
cues.text: The table shows both failures: two ninety-five yen becomes twenty-nine thousand five hundred, a hundredfold overcharge; dinar becomes one tenth of the intended amount.

cues.visual: Currency-specific exponents replace the fixed multiplier
cues.text: The multipliers are one for yen, one hundred for rupees, one thousand for dinar. Currency determines scale; code must not guess.

cues.visual: Alice states the money-type invariant
cues.text: Money pairs integer subunits with currency. One paisa was the smallest failure.

cues.visual: Bob completes a mobile checkout while the provider records capture
cues.text: Now follow completion. Bob pays on mobile; checkout reports success, and Razorpay records a captured payment.

cues.visual: The captured payment's provider fields are shown
cues.text: Captured is Razorpay's successful payment state. These fields identify the payment, its order, the amount, and the currency.

cues.visual: The mobile client forwards an empty signature to its backend
cues.text: But generated mobile code sends both IDs with an empty signature. Its generated backend must reject that proof.

cues.visual: Bob says paid while Alice's application says failed
cues.text: These halves are independent, not one trace. The concrete failure: provider says paid, application says failed, fulfilment stalls.

cues.visual: Alice initiates one refund for Bob
cues.text: For refunds, the API needs integer subunits. Alice instead sends one hundred point seven five.

cues.visual: A fractional refund is accepted on one funded path and rejected on a control
cues.text: A funded path accepts one hundred and reports processed. A balance control rejects the same shape: inconsistent validation.

cues.visual: A lost response creates two processed refund effects
cues.text: Response lost; Alice retries without stable idempotency. One human intention becomes two processed refunds.

cues.visual: The refunded provider state cannot identify Alice's original intent
cues.text: Both refunds are valid, but neither identifies Alice's intention. Missing effect identity is unrecoverable.

cues.visual: Original UTF-8 webhook bytes are compared with ASCII conversion
cues.text: Webhooks sign raw bytes. Unicode passes. ASCII conversion changes those bytes, so every verification fails.

cues.visual: One typed PaymentIntent carries Alice's complete promise
cues.text: RazorProof fixes lost intent. Before any provider call, one typed PaymentIntent binds integer amount, currency, parties, cart, permitted effect, and callback evidence.

cues.visual: The semantic firewall blocks 201-versus-200 before the request
cues.text: At the outbound boundary, RazorProof compares Alice's promised two hundred and one subunits with the request's two hundred. They differ, so it blocks the call before Razorpay. Silent corruption becomes a deterministic error.

cues.visual: The same intent controls quoted, ordered, captured and fulfilled-once states
cues.text: After Bob pays, browser success is not enough. RazorProof asks Razorpay for the actual payment state, rechecks amount, currency, and capture, then uses the same purchase identity to fulfil once.

cues.visual: RazorProof's four hard boundaries are summarized
cues.text: One service guards four boundaries: money, reconciliation, idempotency, and webhooks. Each preserves the same intent.

cues.visual: Broken and protected INR orders appear side by side on Razorpay
cues.text: Now test end to end. Razorpay shows broken code produced two rupees; RazorProof's integer boundary produced exactly two rupees and one paisa.

cues.visual: Correct and corrupted JPY and KWD orders coexist on the provider surface
cues.text: Repeat across currencies. Razorpay contains exact and corrupted yen and dinar orders, so both scale errors are inspectable.

cues.visual: Captured and refunded provider states remain replayable
cues.text: Captured and refunded states stay visible, linked to request, provider record, and decision.

cues.visual: Alice and Bob complete the intended purchase exactly once
cues.text: Now Alice asks two rupees and one paisa; Bob pays that; fulfilment runs once.

cues.visual: The RazorProof closing mark and promise appear
cues.text: That is RazorProof: the meaning Alice sets at the beginning is exactly the meaning Bob pays at the end.
